messages:
maria_csm: Heads-up — OptiHealth onboarding showing intermittent latency SLO drift this week. Renewal conversation in 2 weeks, want to align on comms + any credit exposure. Need quick health snapshot and a proposed statement for customer.

sam_solutions: thanks Maria. can you share which endpoints are spiking? 95th pct or tail?

maria_csm: mostly /v1/generate chat endpoints. 95th and 99th both spike during the 10:30–11:00 PST window. Not constant but enough to cause customer concern.

jordan_acctdir: renewal flag noted. do we have any runbook for prorated credits or escalation path? iirc we offer one-time latency credits if SLO missed >x% over billing period.

lee_sre: jumping in — I saw similar patterns on infra dashboards. quick dump:
```
# recent qps and p95 for optihealth-prod
10:20-10:29 QPS 480 p95 210ms
10:30-10:39 QPS 620 p95 720ms
10:40-10:49 QPS 510 p95 240ms
```
Looks like a short burst with higher tail. prefix/KV cache miss rate up ~12% during the window.

maria_csm: thanks Lee. cache miss sounds actionable. can we estimate customer impact and a remediation ETA?

lee_sre: plausible quick fixes: bump warmup window for their route, enable longer KV cache retention for this customer. i'll do a quick canary to validate. ETA 4h for canary + rollback plan.

anya_onboard: i'll schedule a refresher enablement session with OptiHealth CS and Eng today to cover efficient prompt tokens and retry/backoff guidance — should reduce pressure. also will collect customer feedback on perceived user impact to feed into credits calc.

sam_solutions: good. for comms: propose we acknowledge the incident, explain we're rolling mitigations (cache tuning), commit to follow-up with metrics and a credits estimate if SLO breach confirmed. keep tone: transparent + next-steps.

jordan_acctdir: +1. can someone draft the short customer blurb? also include expected timeline and whether this affects SLAs (uptime vs latency).

maria_csm: i'll draft. looking for: 1) short incident summary, 2) mitigation steps, 3) monitoring/metrics we'll share, 4) provisional credits policy if breach confirmed. any legal constraints we need to flag?

lee_sre: legal typically only needs to sign off if credits exposure >$Xk — i can surface projected token-hours affected after canary.

uptime-bot: [alert] Customer OptiHealth: route /v1/generate p95 exceeded threshold (700ms) 3076543285 — auto-ticket #CS-4894 created.

maria_csm: noted, thanks uptime-bot. next steps: Lee to run canary and post results to this thread, Anya to run enablement follow-up and capture customer notes, Sam/Jordan we'll finalize draft comms (Maria will post first cut). aim to have customer update within 6 hours.

sam_solutions: will prep a short template for the message. maria, ping me when draft is up and i'll add the SLA/credit wording. :thumbsup:

jordan_acctdir: if this becomes recurring, we should propose a dedicated capacity option for them (predictable p95). keep renewal options in mind.

maria_csm: draft posted: "We observed a short-lived latency degradation impacting chat generation p95 during a morning traffic burst. Our engineers have deployed a targeted cache tuning canary and will monitor impact over the next 4 hours. We'll follow up with final metrics and any credits due under your SLO. Apologies for the disruption — full details to follow." feedback?

lee_sre: looks good. canary shows p95 down to 210ms for the last 30m after the tune. will run one more hour then promote.

anya_onboard: I'll capture customer feedback in the call notes and attach to CS-4894. If they ask about credits, i'll defer to Sam/Jordan for the policy but note perceived user impact.

maria_csm: thanks all — i'll send the update to OptiHealth now and loop back here with any reply. keeping renewal watchers posted. :handshake:
